newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Defiant Sierra Leone coupmakers seek deal.
newsitem.headline: Defiant Sierra Leone coupmakers seek deal.

text.p: Sierra Leone's military coup makers and their rebel allies have told Nigeria, West Africa's regional power broker, that it would have to use force to reinstate toppled civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.

But a spokesman also said they wanted a negotiated settlement to avert a bloody showdown and had sent envoys to Ivory Coast to ask its president, Henri Konan Bedie, to intervene to help to find a solution.
The chief of defence staff, Brigadier Samuel Koroma, told a Thursday news conference they had sent a message to Nigerian military leader General Sani Abacha via a delegation he sent to talk to them.
"We have sent a message... saying that General Abacha must choose between peace in Sierra Leone or the forced return of President Kabbah to power by Nigeria and ECOMOG," he said.
Nigeria, which already had troops of the West African ECOMOG force in Freetown under a defence agreement, has been steadily building up its force in the capital since the May 25 coup.
"We are not prepared to hand over to former president Kabbah," Koroma said. "If president Kabbah takes over again, he will jeopardise the peace that we have been able to achieve with the RUF rebels."
Foday Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front has been fighting a bush war since 1991. A peace accord signed with Kabbah last November failed to hold and the rebels have now joined the coup.
The coup leader, Major Johnny Paul Koromah, named Sankoh as vice-chairman in his Armed Forces Revolutionary Council (AFRC).
The council's secretary general, Andrew Koroma, told Reuters a six-man delegation led by Sierra Leone's ambassador to Guinea, Colonel Mohamed Diaby, had left by military helicopter for Ivory Coast.
The aim, he said, was to ask Bedie "to step in to resolve the present impasse between between the AFRC and ECOMOG in order to resolve this situation by negotiations and not by armed confrontation."
Bedie helped to broker a fragile peace in Sierra Leone last year. Diaby was kidnapped by rebels in the east in March and was freed only after the coup.
Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on Monday in a show of force, while rebels attacked Nigerian troops guarding foreigners.

Brigadier Koroma said the military would overthrow Kabbah again if Nigerian-led forces restored him to power, but he promised that the revolutionary council would organise elections within 18 months to two years "for the people to choose the leader they want."
Local politicians in impoverished Sierra Leone, which has suffered three coups in five years, have rejected that idea out of hand.

A summit meeting of the Organisation of African Unity summit, which ended in Harare on Wednesday, called for restoration of Kabbah, who was elected in March 1996 after four years of army rule. He is now in neighbouring Guinea.
Thousands of people have fled the capital for the provinces. The military say 80 people were killed in the clashes on Monday, while other sources put the number at less than 50.
Long queues formed outside the few shops that opened on Thursday as supplies of staples such as rice ran short.
